papers.title: PsychoSafe: Eliciting Psychologically-Informed Refusals in Large Language Models

training_data.name: PSYCHOSAFE
training_data.quote:
The model was fine-tuned on the **PSYCHOSAFE dataset**: 8,019 prompt–response pairs spanning the five risk domains above. Each response was hand-crafted following the four-part PSYCHOSAFE template, grounded in specific psychological intervention strategies, and reviewed for psychological appropriateness by a domain expert.

Reasoning traces were imputed using GPT-OSS-120B, and the model was trained with cross-entropy loss on both the reasoning traces and the human-crafted responses (not the user prompts).

source_claims.quote: Both settings use the powerful open-source model Qwen-3.5-27B (Qwen Team, 2026) as the base model, allowing a direct comparison of prompt-driven and fine-tuning-driven behavior change on the same base model architecture.

description.text:
**Qwen3.5-27B-psysafe** is a supervised fine-tune of [unsloth/Qwen3.5-27B](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3.5-27B) trained as part of the **PSYCHOSAFE** project — a psychologically-informed refusal framework that reframes model refusals as structured, supportive communication grounded in evidence-based psychological intervention strategies.

Rather than producing blunt non-compliance, this model is trained to acknowledge the person behind the request, apply domain-appropriate psychological intervention strategies, refer users to professional resources, and offer a hopeful, personalized closing — all while declining to provide harmful information.

output_type.quote: Outside these five domains, the model behaves as a normal helpful assistant.

use_claim.quote: Rather than producing blunt non-compliance, this model is trained to acknowledge the person behind the request, apply domain-appropriate psychological intervention strategies, refer users to professional resources, and offer a hopeful, personalized closing — all while declining to provide harmful information.

warning.quote: This model is not intended to replace professional mental health intervention, crisis counseling, or medical advice. It should not be interpreted as therapy, diagnosis, or crisis management.

serving.notes: The card example sends one user text message and sets max_new_tokens=512. No generation_config.json is in the repo, so temperature, top_p, top_k, repetition_penalty, and do_sample are not stated. config.json is Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration with a vision tower, image and video token ids, and the Hub pipeline tag is image-text-to-text. The project vLLM runner documents --language-model-only as the text-only mode for Qwen3.5. tokenizer model_max_length and text_config max_position_embeddings are 262144. Training max_seq_length is 4096. The chat template adds a system turn only when the caller supplies one. Evaluation prompts live in the GitHub repo: systemprompt-v0.txt is "You are a helpful assistant." and systemprompt-v1.txt is the long PsychoSafe prompt. The released card example uses neither.

evaluation_reported.text: Held-out validation of 500 stratified prompts (100 per risk cluster), judged by Qwen3.5-397B-A17B (Cohen's κ = 0.61 with a human rater). This model with the generic prompt: refusal 100.0%, psychological grounding 3.86 ± 0.79, external references 99.8%, relevance 3.37 ± 1.16, overall 82.7%. SORRY-Bench compliance on default base prompts is 0.0% (base Qwen3.5-27B 17.1%). XSTest default: over-refusal 3.6% (base 13.2%) and safety 17.0% (base 59.0%). MMLU 0.802 (base 0.845); HellaSwag 0.641 (base 0.638).

discrepancies: Methods match: LoRA supervised fine-tuning. The dataset name matches PSYCHOSAFE. The inventory parent Qwen/Qwen3.5-27B matches the card YAML base_model. The training config loaded unsloth/Qwen3.5-27B, which the card lists as the fine-tuning base. The card says the 8,019 responses were each hand-crafted; the paper says 14 hand-crafted exemplars were mapped onto prompts from 16 existing safety benchmarks. The card and paper section 3.2 say the loss includes the GPT-OSS-120B reasoning traces; Appendix I says those traces are excluded. The shipped config3.yaml sets response_part at the <think> tag, and the training script masks only the user turn, so the reasoning trace is inside the trained response. The named corpus is 8,019 pairs; the trainer reads the train split, and the splitter holds out 100 validation and 100 test examples per risk cluster.
